title: Isolation of human cutaneous immune cells for single-cell RNA sequencing
protocol: Transfer the biopsy to a sterile cell culture dish.
Remove all subcutaneous fat and hair from the biopsy using scissors.
Add 2 mL of enzymatic digestion buffer to a 6-well plate.
Transfer the biopsy to the well containing 2 mL of digestion buffer.
Mince the tissue with scissors for 4 minutes.
Add 2 mL of digestion buffer into the well containing minced tissue to bring the total volume to 4 mL.
Incubate at 37°C with 5% CO₂ overnight for a minimum of 16 hours and a maximum of 18 hours.
Cool all buffers, centrifuges, and cells on ice or at 4°C to maintain cell viability.
Obtain a single-cell suspension after enzymatic dissociation is complete.
Process the cells efficiently to prepare them for flow cytometry sorting.
Stain the single-cell suspension for CD45+ immune cells.
Gently pipette up and down 6–8 times in the 6-well plate containing the digested biopsy using a 5 mL serological pipette.
Transfer the mixed solution to a 50 mL conical tube.
Rinse the same well with 4 mL of cold wash buffer and transfer to the same 50 mL conical tube.
Vigorously shake the tube for 30 seconds.
Pre-wet a 100 μm filter with 1 mL of wash buffer over a new 50 mL conical tube.
Pour the cell solution through the filter into the new 50 mL tube.
Rinse the original conical tube with 5 mL of wash buffer and pour over the filter to wash the filter.
Allow the liquid to filter through thoroughly before removing and discarding the strainer.
Centrifuge the new conical tube containing the single cell suspension at 400 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Decant by pouring supernatant out, leaving approximately 100–200 μL of volume remaining.
Resuspend cells in the remaining volume.
Transfer the resuspended cells to a 96-well V-bottom plate.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Obtain a 7.5 μL aliquot of the cell suspension.
Add an equal amount of 0.4% Trypan Blue Solution to the aliquot.
Gently mix the mixture.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Transfer 10 μL of the mixture to a hemocytometer chamber.
Centrifuge the 96-well plate at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant by tipping over the plate.
Resuspend the cells with 100 μL of antibody cocktail.
Prepare the antibody cocktail containing 97 μL of Cell Staining Buffer and 3 μL of CD45 Mouse Anti-Human APC (approximately a 1:30 dilution).
Incubate the antibody cocktail for 30 min at 4°C in the dark.
Incubate cells in the dark and protected from excess light downstream.
Add 150 μl of FACS buffer and pipette up and down three times to mix.
Centrifuge the plate at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant by tipping over.
Resuspend with 200 μl of FACS buffer and pipette up and down to resuspend three times.
Centrifuge the plate again at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant by tipping over.
Resuspend cells in 200 μl FACS buffer.
Transfer cells to a filtered FACS tube using the same pipette tip to filter the cells before sorting.
Wash the original well with 200 μl of FACS buffer and pass through the same filter.
Fill a new 5 ml FACS tube with 3 ml of Cell Staining Buffer to collect sorted cells.
Prepare your flow cytometry gating workflow.
Test your DAPI concentration on optimization/test skin samples prior to obtaining patient biopsies.
Proceed directly to the next section on Cell Sorting for CD45+ Cells with Flow Cytometry if you have completed this workflow and created a gating template.
Set a sorting gate to capture cells on the Forward Scatter (FSC) versus Side Scatter (SSC) plot.
Create a FSC-Area versus FSC-Width plot to exclude doublets.
Utilize a SSC-A versus SSC-H gate to further exclude any remaining doublets.
Plot singlets on a DAPI-A versus SSC-A plot.
Create a gate to exclude DAPI-positive cells.
Ensure live cells are DAPI-negative.
Add DAPI for a final concentration of 1 μL per 1 million cells.
Test the DAPI concentration to ensure high viability.
Plot live, single cells on a SSC-A versus CD45+ APC plot.
Create a sorting gate for CD45+ cells.
Alternatively, plot DAPI versus APC on a singular plot.
Create a sort layout to sort the live, single, CD45+ cells.
Isolate less abundant immune cell subpopulation using BD FACSAria Fusion Cell Sorter.
Ensure high cell viability by eliminating poor-quality cells and debris.
Collect all sorted CD45+ cells, accounting for potential cell loss in later wash steps.
Conduct optimization experiments to set PMT voltages before obtaining patient biopsies.
Create a gating template based on single-stained samples for accurate flow sorting.
Ensure the cytometer has been turned on and calibrated before sorting cells.
Set the sorting pressure to the lowest setting.
Open the previously created gating template.
Add DAPI to the sample, flick mix, and incubate for 5 minutes.
Sort into a collection tube containing 3 mL of Cell Staining Buffer.
Conduct sorting under the lowest pressure and flow settings.
Add FACS buffer to the sorting tube to reach a total volume of 5 mL.
Resuspend the cells by washing the sides of the FACS tube with FACS buffer.
Centrifuge the tube at 400 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant by pouring it off.
Centrifuge the tube again at 400 g for 1 additional minute at 4°C.
Resuspend the cells in the remaining volume and transfer to a 96-well v-bottom plate.
Spin the plate at 400 g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Decant the supernatant by tipping over the plate.
Add 10 μL of Cell Staining Buffer to achieve a total volume of approximately 41 μL.
Resuspend the cells and transfer them to a Low Retention 0.8 mL Microcentrifuge Tube.

Perform a final cell count using a hemocytometer: take a 7.5 μL aliquot of cells, combine with 7.5 μL of Trypan Blue Solution (0.4%), gently mix, incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes, and then transfer 10 μL to the hemocytometer chamber.
Adjust the cell concentration to 700-1,200 cells/μL with Cell Staining Buffer if necessary.
Perform an additional cell count after dilution.
Proceed to the desired single-cell RNA-sequencing library construction protocol.
Utilize 20,000 read pairs/cell for Single Cell 3′ v3.1 libraries and Single Cell 5′ v2 libraries as recommended by 10× Genomics.
Minimize post-sorting time before utilizing cells for library preparation.
Quantify and assess the quality of scRNA-seq libraries using the High Sensitivity DNA assay on the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer.
Use either KAPA Library Quantification kit or a Qubit fluorometer for quantification.
